title: Nephron Anatomy: Glomerulus, Loop of Henle & Collecting
description: Master nephron anatomy inside the kidney, from the glomerulus and podocyte filtration barrier to the proximal tubule, loop of Henle, and collecting tubule.
h1: Nephron Microanatomy: Renal Corpuscle, Filtration Barrier and Tubules
blurb: From the fenestrated glomerulus and podocyte filtration slits through the proximal tubule, countercurrent loop of Henle, macula densa, and collecting duct.
lead: Each kidney contains roughly one million microscopic nephrons—tiny biological purifying plants that filter blood plasma under pressure and selectively reclaim vital solutes. In this illustrated guide to nephron kidney microanatomy, we examine 20 documented structures—including afferent arteriole, glomerular capillaries, efferent arteriole, bowman capsule—linking regional topography, tissue architecture, physiological mechanisms, and clinical reasoning.
overview: Each kidney contains roughly one million microscopic nephrons—tiny biological purifying plants that filter blood plasma under pressure and selectively reclaim vital solutes. Each nephron begins with a glomerular capillary tuft inside Bowman capsule; the filtration barrier includes fenestrated endothelium, glomerular basement membrane and podocyte slit diaphragms. Filtrate enters proximal tubule, descends and ascends in the loop of Henle, then passes distal tubule into a collecting duct. Collecting ducts arise from a different embryologic lineage than nephron tubules. Peritubular capillaries and vasa recta reclaim water and solutes; juxtaglomerular apparatus links distal salt sensing to renin secretion. Within the human body, the nephron · kidney microanatomy (Nephron · corpusculum renale) is situated in renal cortex (corpuscle and convoluted tubules) → medulla (loop and collecting system), receives arterial perfusion via afferent arteriole → glomerulus → efferent arteriole → peritubular capillaries/vasa recta, and is innervated by renal sympathetic fibers reach vasculature, juxtaglomerular cells and tubules.

Structurally, the afferent arteriole (Arteriola afferens) comprises brings arterial blood into glomerular capillary tuft. Physiologically, the afferent arteriole regulates incoming glomerular pressure. Structurally, the glomerular capillaries (Glomerulus) comprises fenestrated capillary loops between afferent and efferent arterioles. Physiologically, the glomerular capillaries pass plasma water and small solutes toward Bowman space. Structurally, the efferent arteriole (Arteriola efferens) comprises vessel leaves glomerulus and feeds downstream capillary network. Physiologically, the efferent arteriole maintains filtration pressure and supplies cortical/medullary beds. Structurally, the Bowman capsule (Capsula glomeruli) comprises parietal squamous layer and visceral podocyte layer enclosing Bowman space. Physiologically, the Bowman capsule collects primary filtrate from glomerulus. The filtration basement membrane (Membrana basalis glomerularis) is specialized basement membrane shared by capillary endothelium and podocytes. Physiologically, the filtration basement membrane governs contributes size/charge selectivity. Structurally, the podocyte foot processes (Pedicelli podocytorum) comprises interdigitating podocyte extensions with slit diaphragms over glomerular capillaries. Physiologically, the podocyte foot processes governs final cellular component of filtration barrier.

Clinically, regarding the afferent arteriole, diameter influences filtration rate. From a diagnostic standpoint, in the glomerular capillaries, damage may permit albumin or red cells into urine. In clinical pathology involving the efferent arteriole, unique arteriole between two capillary beds. Medical evaluation of the Bowman capsule also notes that filtrate flows from urinary pole to proximal tubule.

questions.question: What are the main parts of a nephron?
questions.answer: A renal corpuscle filters plasma; proximal tubule, loop of Henle and distal tubule modify filtrate. Collecting ducts receive fluid from multiple nephrons.

questions.question: Where does filtration occur in the kidney?
questions.answer: Filtration occurs across glomerular capillaries into Bowman’s space in renal corpuscles, mainly in the kidney cortex.

questions.question: What is Bowman’s capsule?
questions.answer: Bowman’s capsule has a parietal squamous layer and a visceral podocyte layer enclosing Bowman’s space.

questions.question: Where are the podocyte foot processes located?
questions.answer: Podocyte foot processes cover the outer surface of glomerular capillaries and form filtration slits facing Bowman’s space.

questions.question: What is the function of the collecting duct?
questions.answer: The collecting duct adjusts water reabsorption in response to antidiuretic hormone and contributes to acid–base regulation.
